series.title: III. Life in the Covenant and Service
IV. Prophecies and the Hope of the End
V. Life and Emotions - practical module

studies.title: Does God care about me?
studies.summary: A first encounter with a God who knows me personally, who made me out of love and cares about my everyday life - a starting point for a relationship, not for religion.

studies.title: Who really is Jesus?
studies.summary: Who Jesus of Nazareth really is: a historical figure and at the same time the eternal God, the Creator who became human to save me and reveal the Father - and who he wants to be for me personally.

studies.title: Where do evil and suffering come from?
studies.summary: If God is good and almighty, where does evil come from? The Bible answers not with philosophy, but with the story of the great controversy: a world created good, love that requires freedom, rebellion in heaven, the fall of humanity - and a God who is not the author of evil, but the One who resolves it on the cross.

studies.title: Why did Jesus have to die?
studies.summary: Sin is not just a list of bad deeds, but a broken bond with God - lost trust, out of which specific sins grow. The result is separation and death, and God's answer is the cross: Jesus took my place to restore the relationship. Obedience is the fruit of reconciliation, not its condition.

studies.title: A gift you can't buy
studies.summary: Salvation is a gift of grace received through faith, not a reward earned by works. God justifies the sinner and gives the assurance of eternal life right now - an assurance grounded in Christ, not in my own sinlessness. Works are the fruit of salvation, never its price.

studies.title: How to start over?
studies.summary: Conversion is not self-improvement, but a change of direction: repentance and the surrender of your life to God, in which he gives you new birth, a new heart, and makes you a new creation. It is the beginning of a relationship renewed every day, not a one-time act to be checked off.

studies.title: The Holy Spirit in my life
studies.summary: The Holy Spirit is not an impersonal "energy," but a Person and God - the third Person of the Trinity. He guides, comforts, convicts of sin, gives power to live, and bears the fruit of character. We come to know him as an ever-present Companion, with whom we can be filled.

studies.title: How to talk with God?
studies.summary: Prayer is not a magic formula or a religious duty, but an honest conversation with God, who hears and answers. We learn to talk with a Friend simply, regularly, and with trust - and we discover that prayer changes us and our circumstances.

studies.title: The Bible - God's voice to me
studies.summary: The Bible is the inspired Word of God - a letter from a Friend, not a collection of human opinions. We learn where its authority comes from (sola scriptura), pick up simple principles for reading it on your own, and discover where it is best to begin. The PRO layer addresses the question of Scripture and Tradition, and of the canon.

studies.title: Temptation, falling, forgiveness
studies.summary: The struggle with temptation is a normal part of the life of faith, not proof of failure. We learn to overcome in the power of Jesus, and after a fall to return through confession and accepting forgiveness. God does not reject the one who falls - we distinguish between a stumble and deliberately remaining in sin, and we learn to forgive ourselves and others.

studies.title: Jesus' greatest promise
studies.summary: The return of Jesus is the promise and the heart of Christian hope. We learn the certainty of this promise and the signs of the times, and especially the character of His coming: visible, audible, global, and final - "every eye will see Him." We respond to mistaken ideas of a "secret rapture" and an "invisible presence." This is hope, not a reason for fear.

studies.title: Hope stronger than death
studies.summary: The Bible speaks of death as a "sleep" from which the resurrection awakens us when Jesus returns - this is hope, not a reason for fear. We explore this teaching, a warning against spiritism and "contacting the dead," and the biblical answer to reincarnation. The PRO layer addresses the doctrine of purgatory and prayers for the dead.

studies.title: Life in God's family
studies.summary: The church is not a building but a family and the body of Christ - a place of community, support, and growth. We explore the meaning of belonging, the unity expressed in obedience to Christ the Head, and the Lord's Supper as a memorial of his sacrifice, with the ordinance of humility. Additional layers: discerning God's will, and the Supper as a memorial in light of the Mass and transubstantiation.

studies.title: A decision that changes life
studies.summary: Baptism is a public confession of faith and an identification with the death and resurrection of Jesus - believer's baptism by immersion. We speak gently about "rebaptism" after a childhood baptism, emphasizing that it is a declaration of readiness, not haste, and that the strength to persevere comes from Jesus himself. This closes the series and is an invitation to the daily decision to walk with God.

studies.title: The God who keeps his word
studies.summary: From creation, God binds himself to humanity through covenant; when we fall, he seeks us out and renews his promise - because he always keeps his word. Here the heart of the great controversy is laid bare: can God be trusted? The blood of Jesus is the new covenant, and the Ten Commandments are a revelation of God's character, not legalism.

studies.title: Why do we need commandments?
studies.summary: The Bible distinguishes the moral law (the Ten Commandments - enduring, because it expresses God's character) from the ceremonial law of Moses (which pointed to Christ and was fulfilled in him). Keeping the commandments is not legalism, but obedience born of love and in the power of the Spirit - relationship before rules.

studies.title: The Sabbath - time with God
studies.summary: The Sabbath was instituted already at creation, for all people, as a memorial of the Creator and a weekly gift of relationship and freedom. The fourth commandment, which Jesus himself kept, leads to rest in Christ - not a burden, but a space to meet with God.

studies.title: Jesus - our High Priest
studies.summary: The earthly sanctuary was a model of the plan of salvation: its sacrifices pointed to Jesus the Lamb, and its priesthood to his ministry. Today Jesus is the High Priest in the heavenly sanctuary - our only Mediator. The sanctuary is linked with the covenant: the law in the ark, grace on the mercy seat; we have sure access to God.

studies.title: God's principles of health
studies.summary: The body is a gift from God and a temple of the Spirit. We approach health holistically: nutrition, exercise, rest, water, sunlight, temperance, and trust in God, along with our emotions, forgiveness, gratitude, joy, and service. The "Blue Zones" (including Loma Linda) show that God's principles for living truly serve a long life.

studies.title: Spiritual gifts in service
studies.summary: God equips every believer for service. The Spirit distributes different gifts, and one body - the Church - joins them into a whole. Everyone is to discover and use their gift. The Bible also gives criteria for recognizing a true gift and a true prophet. The gift of healing reminds us that God acts today - within His will and the mystery of suffering. The goal of all the gifts: building up the Church.

studies.title: My mission and talents
studies.summary: Everything belongs to God - I am a steward, not an owner. Faithful stewardship covers time, abilities, and money (tithe and offerings) and flows from gratitude, not compulsion. Out of this is born my personal and local mission: how I concretely serve God and people in my community and surroundings.

studies.title: World history in prophecy
studies.summary: Nebuchadnezzar's dream in Daniel 2 shows that God knows and guides the course of history: empire after empire will pass away, but His eternal Kingdom - the "stone" - will remain. Fulfilled prophecy becomes a solid foundation for trusting the Bible.

studies.title: 70 weeks and 2300 days
studies.summary: Daniel's numerical prophecies - 70 weeks and 2300 days - read by the day-year principle. The 70 weeks point precisely to the Messiah (proof that Jesus is the Christ), and the 2300 days lead to the year 1844 and open up the theme of the cleansing of the heavenly sanctuary and the judgment.

studies.title: Apocalyptic beasts and the Lamb
studies.summary: Daniel 7 retells the line of empires in the language of beasts, and the "little horn" foretells a religious-political power active through a period of 1260 day-years (Dan 7:25; Rev 12; 13). This is a prophecy about domination and persecution - but its heart is the Lamb, who conquers and takes possession of the eternal kingdom.

studies.title: Why is the judgment good news?
studies.summary: The three angels' messages proclaim that "the hour of judgment has come" - in the context of the eternal gospel and a call to worship the Creator. The investigative judgment of Daniel 7 is not meant to frighten: in heaven Jesus is our Advocate, and those who believe in Him are safe.

studies.title: God's church in the last days
studies.summary: Prophecy does not only describe the powers hostile to God - it also shows where His faithful people are in the last days: the remnant, who keep the commandments, hold the testimony of Jesus and have the gift of prophecy, and whose distinguishing mark is a global mission of proclaiming Christ's return.

studies.title: Jesus' coming and the millennium
studies.summary: A deeper look at the second coming: it will be visible, audible, glorious and global. It is accompanied by the resurrection of the righteous and the transformation of the living, and then a thousand years (the millennium) - the saved in heaven, an emptied earth, Satan bound, and judgment on the wicked.

studies.title: A new heaven and a new earth
studies.summary: The finale of the great controversy: sin, death and evil are destroyed forever, and God creates a new heaven and a new earth. No tears, pain or death, with Eden restored and an eternal, close relationship with God - this is the goal of the whole journey and an open invitation.

studies.title: Your true worth
studies.summary: Where my sense of worth comes from and who has the right to tell me who I am. Despite childhood wounds, comparisons and a sense of inferiority, God calls me his child, made on purpose, treasured and accepted in Christ.

studies.title: Conflicts and reconciliation
studies.summary: What to do with the wounds, bitterness and conflicts between people. How to understand forgiveness (which is not pretending nothing happened), how to resolve disputes God's way, and how not to let anger turn into bitterness.

studies.title: Peace that surpasses understanding
studies.summary: What Scripture says about worry, anxiety and being overwhelmed - and how a peace is born that "surpasses all understanding." It is not about suppressing emotions but about shifting the weight onto God, who knows our needs and is near.

studies.title: Hope in sorrow and loneliness
studies.summary: For the days when it is hard, empty or dark. Scripture is not ashamed of sorrow or loneliness - it shows a God who is near to the broken in spirit, and people of faith who went through the depths. About hope, community, and the truth that seeking help is not a lack of faith.

studies.title: Joy beyond circumstances
studies.summary: About a joy that does not depend on circumstances, about giving thanks "in every situation," and about where to look for meaning in life. Gratitude and joy in the Lord are not naive optimism - they are attitudes that genuinely change the heart and give direction to everyday life.

studies.title: Freedom in everyday choices
studies.summary: What true freedom is - not "do whatever you want," but release from what enslaves us: addictions, the power of money, pressure, and the compulsion of sin. How Christ sets us free, how to master ourselves as the fruit of the Spirit, and how to make everyday choices (money, work) as a free person.

studies.title: How to know God's will?
studies.summary: How to make decisions and discern God's guidance - without the magic of "signs" and without the paralysis of fear. About trust, a renewed mind, the role of the Word, prayer, circumstances, and community, and about how a readiness to obey opens up knowledge of God's will.
